tagline: A phone snap becomes a product image you can use.
brief: Product concept: a photo editor for small online sellers. Turn an ordinary phone photo into a clean product image, compare backgrounds, and export a version for a listing or social post.
promise: Turn a phone photo into a cleaner product image
question: How can the same product prove the improvement before the feature explanation?
overview: Three source demonstrations show a visible input, editing steps, and a finished product image. Lead with the before and after, keep the object recognizable, then show enough of the workflow to make the change understandable. Product photos is an illustrative product concept, not a claim about a released app. Source views and interactions describe the indexed posts; they do not establish sales, conversion, organic reach, or editing accuracy.
searchNotes: Reuse-first research followed by compact caption and transcript searches. Full detail was reserved for finalists.
All 24 gokceercan, 32 photoshop._blog, and 33 spk3241_ indexed frames were visually inspected. These references show real people or hands and are not people-free examples.
spk3241_ has a Thai caption and unrelated song transcript. Its relevance comes from the inspected interface and product frames, not a translated testimonial.
Promotional captions and discount codes are retained as source evidence. The suggested storyboard makes no time-saving or sales guarantee.

angles.title: Let the same object prove the change.
angles.label: BEFORE AND AFTER
angles.description: Open with the original snap beside the edited result. Keep the crop and object recognizable so the viewer can judge the improvement.
angles.whyItFits: A seller can see what the editor changes before hearing a feature list.
angles.evidence: gokceercan compares the same bag at 3.2s. spk3241_ shows a grey-surface toothbrush at 3.93s and the white-background output at 21.13s. No sales outcome is measured.
angles.suggestedHook: Same product. Which photo would you put in your listing?
angles.visualDirection: Start with a labeled original and edited image. Keep product details visible and use actual app output.

angles.title: Replace the setup montage with a visible workflow.
angles.label: SHOW THE STEPS
angles.description: Show the inconvenient starting photo, then import, edit, compare, and export. Finish on the usable image.
angles.whyItFits: The workflow explains the proposed product through an observable task.
angles.evidence: photoshop._blog shows props before Product Staging at 15.37s. gokceercan shows import at 12.6s, background editing at 14.8s, and a share view at 21.8s.
angles.suggestedHook: Start with the photo you already have.
angles.visualDirection: One original photo stays in view while the actual editing steps produce a new background. Avoid invented processing-time counters.
